_comment: The hazard model's numbers (core/hazardModel.ts). EVERY value here is a gameRule: tuned so Panaji plays as a fair build-and-protect game. None is a measurement or claims to come from a study. Water is in 'game metres', compared with the DEM ground height of each tile; the real Panaji ground is real, the water is game design.

surge._comment: Cyclone storm surge. Level at the landfall site = baseM + perStrengthM x strength. Each hex the water moves it loses: seaM along the open sea, channelM up a river or creek (it funnels further there), beachM over sand, landM over land. weakStorm: a storm weaker than refStrength loses more height per hex at sea and up the channels, by (refStrength / strength) to the given exponents, so a small cyclone's surge stays near where it comes ashore while the finale (at refStrength) is unchanged. All of it is a game rule.

flood._comment: Monsoon river flood. Sources are the level's own (climate.floodSource in levels.json: Panaji's upstream Mandovi at the east edge of the board, Section 16.5); on a level without one, the upstream part of the river (riverIndex up to sourceShare of the mouth index). Level at a source = baseM + perStrengthM x strength. It loses channelM per hex down the river and creeks, wetlandM per hex into the wetland (khazan) fields, landM per hex up the banks.

compound._comment: Cyclone and flood together. The surge holds the river back at the mouth: every channel tile also gets a backwater level = backwaterShare x (surge level at the mouth) x (riverIndex/mouthIndex)^backwaterExponent on top of the flood's own level there.

defence._comment: A defence protects the area round it: water within radiusHex hexes stands lower by metresPerResilience x its resilience (scaled by maturity and wear) x falloff[distance]. On a tile only the strongest defence of each kind counts; different kinds add up (layered defence), to at most stackCap times the strongest single one there, so a mix of defences does more than many of one kind. pathShare of that also slows water passing through its own tile and its neighbours. Negative resilience (sand mining, a resort) lets water through more easily. Engineered structures fail when the water on their tile is deeper than failureThreshold x failDepthPerUnit, and then give no protection; nature defences over overwhelmSeverity x overwhelmDepthPerUnit protect at their overwhelmed share and are worn. However many defences stand round a tile, together they hold back at most maxProtectionM there (an engineered structure's own protection may reach engineeredMaxProtectionM): the front line of a big storm is lost even behind the best defences, and what a player saves is the streets behind it.

wind._comment: Cyclone wind (Section 12), a game rule, tuned so the surge stays the main threat and the wind decides some homes at the margin. In game metres of water-equivalent: a house falls when the water on its tile plus the wind there reaches houseLossDepthM. perStrengthM x strength on the shore at landfall (x compound.surgeShare in the compound storm), falling off evenly to nothing landfallReachHex hexes from the landfall site, and keeping inlandKeep of itself per hex inland from the open sea; higher ground does not block it. Section 25.1 (owner decision): pandanus (sandy_vegetation) is the only defence that lowers the wind: every tile within shelterReachHex of a pandanus keeps 1 - shelter[kind] of the wind, in any direction; more pandanus round a tile add nothing, and at least minKeep always gets through. Nothing else slows the wind. A flood has no wind.
wind._sandReachComment: Section 34b (owner decision, 28 October 2026), a game rule: a cyclone's wind reaches only the tiles within sandReachHex of a beach tile that can take pandanus; every other tile takes no wind damage (the water is unchanged). So every home the wind can take is one pandanus can shelter.
